policy_floor: a violation of an explicit MUST / never / catastrophic-if-violated invariant: .claude/routed-concerns-software-estate.md row 21 clause (8) (routed-concern table; 'no doc may describe an upgrade path ... as supported behavior')
trigger: an operator with a live earlier-build deployment reads the 0.15.0 release notes and follows CHANGELOG.md:442 (stop every earlier-build replica, then start the first on this release) / :995 ('Upgrades that pass neither parameter are unaffected') / :440 (an earlier-build install's .cfg files are imported at the first boot of this release); these lines were edited by commit 9ab4a8ed1 (pre-6.2 -> earlier-build relabel) and still describe an upgrade path
summary: Agreed HIGH by security-guardian, architect (A1), consistency-auditor (CA-1), release-deploy (REL-2), enterprise-readiness (ER-1) and the unhappy-path derivation; docs-writer rated the same cluster MEDIUM (D3/D4) - the derived band governs, disagreement recorded. Grounding: migrations never refuse a database written by another build (pg_migration_runner skips versions <= schema_meta) so the unsupported path looks healthy; the first-boot .cfg importer still runs (server.cpp:5250), so Gate 2's suggested 'imports no .cfg files' wording is FALSE - do not use it. Proposed text (not applied: the changelog-fragment-guard hook denies agent edits to CHANGELOG.md and its reason makes post-release edits operator-owned). 440 last sentence -> 'If enrollment-tokens.cfg or pending-agents.cfg is present in the data or config directory at first boot, the server imports it once into the database (verified against a stored content fingerprint, so a later mismatched file is refused rather than merged) and renames it aside. The server does not check where such a file came from, and imported tokens and approved agent entries are live credentials: a fresh deployment must not start with these files left over from an earlier install. This is not an upgrade path; this release supports initial deployment into a fresh database only (see Upgrading, Deployment contract).' 442 -> replace by 'Run only one build against a deployment: a replica of an earlier build reads its own .cfg files, not this database, so it neither sees the tokens or approvals held here nor counts their uses.' (no link to #pre-upgrade-checklist). 995 -> delete 'Upgrades that pass neither parameter are unaffected;' (the exit-code 7 and 11 semantics are true vs yuzu-server.iss and stay).
classification_rationale: text describes an upgrade path the hard-cutover contract denies; routed-row floor

trigger: an operator with a live earlier-build stack follows README.md:193 ('Upgrading (... pull && up -d after you change YUZU_VERSION) ... keep the CA and the secrets key'; 'Back up before upgrading') or docs/user-manual/upgrading.md 'Upgrading the Server' ('An upgrade is a pull-and-restart', Docker/Linux/Windows, Upgrade Order, Pre-Upgrade Checklist, Rollback), deploy/docker/docker-compose.reference-gateway.yml 88-91 ('UPGRADING an existing stack'), docs/user-manual/README.md:41, docs/operations/disaster-recovery.md 12-16 and 40, docs/user-manual/server-admin.md Windows in-place upgrade 513-529
summary: Commit 9ab4a8ed1 fixed only the docker-compose.reference.yml header (verified correct and consistent with upgrading.md:599) while the Change Summary's claim 1 requires that no other doc still advertise an upgrade recipe; that claim is FALSE. Not introduced line-by-line by this commit (these lines predate it) but the PR ships them and the owner ruling of 2026-10-24 (row 21 clause 8) is categorical. Class-i operator instructions fully enumerated in the consistency-auditor TSV (scratchpad h-enum-full.tsv). Minimal fix set (enterprise-readiness/architect agree): README.md:193 -> 'Recreating the server keeps the certificate authority and secrets key; changing YUZU_VERSION on an existing install is not a supported upgrade for 0.15.0, which supports fresh deployment only (see Upgrading, Deployment contract).' and drop 'Back up before upgrading'; a banner at the top of upgrading.md and above Upgrade Order / Pre-Upgrade Checklist / Upgrading the Server: 'Fresh deployment only. 0.15.0 supports initial deployment into a freshly provisioned database; it provides no upgrade path from an earlier build's database or backups and no return to an earlier build. The server does not enforce this: migrations do not refuse a database written by another build, and a first-boot importer still reads leftover enrollment-tokens.cfg and pending-agents.cfg files without checking where they came from. Procedures below that describe upgrading, rolling back or restoring an earlier build's data are historical and not supported for 0.15.0.'; delete or reword reference-gateway.yml 88-91 to 'Recreating the containers of this deployment (same volumes): bring up the WHOLE stack ...'; disaster-recovery.md 12-16 add a fresh-database note. Runtime refusals/warnings in yuzu-server.iss, preinst, rpm spec and the service file must stay. Scope of the remaining per-feature notes is hc-3.
classification_rationale: documents an unsupported path as the procedure; routed-row floor

trigger: a fresh Postgres deployment on a host whose data or config directory still holds enrollment-tokens.cfg or pending-agents.cfg from an unrelated earlier install (package removed but not purged, or only the DB volume dropped): the first-boot importer (server.cpp:5250, enrollment_cfg_import.cpp) activates them with no provenance or age check
summary: Chaos S1 (reasoned from code + tests; no server test binary exists locally so not run): imported tokens keep use_count/revoked, expires=0 (never) and max_uses=0 (unlimited) carry over, approved pending agents stay approved; a detective enrollment.import audit row is written, no preventive control. The contract checklist (upgrading.md:599, compose header, CHANGELOG 1361) lists only the database and earlier binaries to exclude, so 'no data imported from earlier builds' is not true of the executable. I7 raises to HIGH (omission conceals security-relevant behaviour); unhappy-path/compliance-officer would hold MEDIUM only if CHANGELOG 440 counts as sufficient disclosure - and hc-1 removes that disclosure unless relocated. Fix requires an OWNER edit of the 2026-10-24 contract text (do not self-edit row 21 or the contract): add 'no enrollment-tokens.cfg or pending-agents.cfg in the data or config directory; review the enrollment.import audit row after first boot' to the checklist, and use the hc-1 440 text.
classification_rationale: contract checklist omits a live credential-import path

summary: Policy floor 'a direct edit to CHANGELOG.md' on its face. Mechanical evidence says the CI 'Changelog fragments' job and --guard see only [Unreleased] and accept the edits; but changelog.d/README.md ('Never edit CHANGELOG.md in a PR') and scripts/hooks/changelog-fragment-guard.py (denies Edit/Write; reason: a fix to an already-released section is operator-owned) carry no carve-out for a post-promote correction, and .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md has no such procedure. The session lead characterised these edits as the sanctioned promote follow-up; that characterisation is not an owner waiver recorded here, and the orchestrator does not self-waive. Needs an explicit owner waiver recorded in this ledger (waiver_rationale) or an owner ruling that the floor does not reach a release-prep branch. Suggested one-sentence addition to changelog.d/README.md: 'A promoted section may be corrected only on the release-prep branch, through review and a governance ledger row; promote --append preserves such edits, and a fresh promote will no longer reproduce them.'
classification_rationale: no documented procedure for post-promote correction; floor needs waiver
